result.summary: Adds a periodic GitHub Actions workflow and helper scripts to detect silent merge conflicts across open pull requests. Every six hours, the workflow fetches non-draft open PRs without git merge conflicts, merges each locally against the latest master branch, runs the build and test suite, and posts the outcome to the PR using GitHub's Checks API.
result.problem: Pull requests can merge cleanly in git without textual conflicts but fail to build or pass tests due to semantic changes merged into master since the branch point. Contributors and maintainers must manually retest or rebase to discover these silent breakages.
evidence: Commit message: 'Adds a periodic CI workflow that runs every 6 hours to detect silent merge failures across all open PRs. For each PR, it fetches the pre-built merge commit (pull/<n>/merge), runs a build and the tests, and posts the result as a check run against the PR's head SHA.'

Description: 'It will look through all open PRs and discard anything that has a git merge failure or a failing test with the thinking that there is no point checking something that can't be merged anyway.'
result.changed_since_previous: The workflow separates candidate evaluation and compilation from status reporting across two distinct jobs with restricted permissions.
result.card: Adds a periodic GitHub Actions workflow and helper scripts to detect silent merge conflicts across open pull requests. The job iterates through candidate PRs, merges them against current master, builds and runs tests via an existing commit execution script, and writes status results via the GitHub Checks API. This automates detection of logical breakages between PRs and master before maintainers attempt to merge them. The change is restricted to CI workflow files and maintenance scripts.

risk.why: Touches only periodic GitHub Actions configuration and repository scripts without impacting release code or developer build environments.
